answer: Distance-to-seed decay resists sybils: influence multiplies by a factor below one for every hop an identity sits from the trusted seed set, so weight falls off geometrically with graph distance. A sybil cluster bolted on far past the tundra, reachable only through a long thin river of edges, inherits a vanishing fraction no matter how it interlinks internally — each hop is another plume of decay. Honest identities cluster close to the seed with short paths and high residual weight; distant fakes decay to near-zero.
